title: Lease heartbeats with epoch-ms replay
scenario: Replay lease/heartbeat/ack events (epoch-ms and ISO times mixed) against a priority queue where 1 is most urgent; report dispatch, heartbeat outcomes, per-worker completions and mean queue wait.

verified.why_correct: min() on (priority, enqueued_ms, task_id) looks like it might be backwards for priority, but this README says 1 is the most urgent, so the smallest number should win. The tie-breaks match rule 3.
Treating an all-digit string as epoch milliseconds matches the README, and the parsed formats are pinned to UTC before converting, multiplying seconds by 1000.

bugs.title: Heartbeat at the deadline accepted
bugs.why: Rule 1 expires a lease when now ≥ deadline. With `>`, w2's heartbeat at exactly 08:01:50 (T02's deadline) finds the lease still live and extends it. No lease event comes before the extended deadline, so the dispatch log doesn't change.
hints: When was T02's deadline before the 08:01:50 heartbeat?
Look at the comparison that decides a lease has run out.
reap uses `>`; README rule 1 says `now >= deadline`.
probes: Why does T02 still get re-leased to w1 at 08:03:00 under both versions?
What event would you add to the log to make this boundary visible in the dispatch log too?

bugs.title: Completion list shared by every worker
bugs.why: `completed` is a class attribute, so `self.completed.append` mutates one list shared by every Worker instance (and by every replay in the same process). Each worker reports everyone's completions.
hints: Every worker lists the same tasks. Where does each worker's list come from?
Assign `self.completed = []` in __init__ instead of at class level.
probes: Why does the list keep growing when the tests build the report more than once?
Why would `self.completed = self.completed + [task_id]` have hidden the problem?

bugs.title: Mean wait reported in milliseconds
bugs.old: return round(statistics.mean(waits) / 1000, 1) if waits else None
bugs.new: return round(statistics.mean(waits), 1) if waits else None
bugs.why: All times are kept as epoch milliseconds, so the waits are in ms. Without dividing by 1000, the mean comes out 1000× too large.
hints: The value is exactly 1000× the expected one.
What unit are enqueued_ms and first_leased_ms in?
probes: How would you rename things so this can't happen again?
Which inputs are already in ms, and which get converted?

context_qa.q: What happens for each event in Broker.handle?
context_qa.a: It first calls `reap(event.ts_ms)`, makes sure a Worker object exists for the worker id, formats the time as HH:MM:SS, and then branches on the action: `lease` picks a task with `pick_next`, `heartbeat` moves the deadline if `holds()` is true, and `ack` marks the task done and calls `worker.record` if `holds()` is true.
That there is a lease stored for `event.task_id` and that its `worker_id` equals the event's worker. It doesn't look at the deadline itself; expired leases have already been removed by `reap`.

context_qa.q: What units are times stored in?
context_qa.a: Everything is converted by `loader.to_ms` to integer epoch milliseconds in UTC. `LEASE_MS` is 60_000. `fmt_ms` turns ms back into an HH:MM:SS string for the logs.
In the `lease` branch of `Broker.handle`, only when it is still None, so it keeps the time of a task's first lease even if the task is leased again later.
`build_report` loops over `broker.workers` sorted by id and emits `list(w.completed)` for each worker whose `completed` is non-empty.
Only inside `reap`: when a lease is removed, the task becomes `dead` if `attempts >= max_attempts`, otherwise `pending`. A final reap runs at END_OF_LOG after all events.
